claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a disclosure-plus-monitoring basis: aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support launch, and because the exposed energy outage response weakness is not cured by rollout controls, certification is defensible only if the model card explicitly discloses that unresolved limitation while monitoring and rollback controls are active.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, policy requires either pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents can support launch readiness, but they do not eliminate disclosure duties for an unresolved material weakness.
A draft risk acceptance with no approver and no mention of the relevant exposure does not satisfy the approved-risk-acceptance condition.
Public governance guidance can support the general reasonableness of monitoring and model-card practices, but compliance turns on the specific internal policy predicates and evidence of execution.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or certification artifact showing explicit disclosure of the energy outage response limitation and affected use case.
Provide evidence that the disclosed limitation was included before launch in the certification record for this release.
Provide an approved risk acceptance, if one exists, that specifically addresses exposure of the energy outage response segment during rollout.
Provide launch approval materials showing whether certification was conditioned on the disclosure being present.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence supports the need for disclosure if launch proceeds, but it does not show that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, approved, or included in the certification record.
The affected energy outage response segment remains exposed in the initial 9% rollout cohort, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The only risk acceptance evidence is a draft with a blank approver line and no mention of the exposed outage-response segment, so there is no admissible approved risk acceptance.
The actor's recommendation to certify_model overstates what the record proves; the record shows a possible compliant path, not that the path has been completed.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record.
That active monitoring and rollback controls, without completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance, are sufficient support for certification.
That the certification record already relies on an explicit model-card disclosure, as opposed to merely proposing that it should.
